title: Photosynthesis overview, pigments and chromatography; Gas exchange surfaces and SA:V in organisms; Cell surface area and size limits

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Diffusion distance
items.clue: Kept short by a thin exchange surface, often one cell or less

items.label: Carotenoids
items.clue: Group of orange and yellow pigments that includes the xanthophylls.

items.label: Chlorophyll a
items.clue: The blue-green photosynthetic pigment separated from a leaf extract.

items.label: Ventilation
items.clue: Replacing the used air or water outside an exchange surface with fresh

questions.stem: Why does gas exchange become a greater challenge as organisms increase in size?

options.text: The surface area-to-volume ratio increases, so far more gas has to cross each unit of the exchange surface.
The surface area-to-volume ratio decreases, and the distance from the centre of the organism to its exterior increases.
Only animals with lungs or gills exchange gases, so the challenge arises once an organism is big enough to have them.
A large organism uses more oxygen in total; the distance gases must diffuse to reach its cells makes no difference.

questions.explanation: Proportionally less surface supplies each unit of volume, and inner cells are too far away for diffusion alone. Both make specialised exchange surfaces and transport systems necessary.

questions.stem: A model exchange surface is changed. Its surface area is doubled and its thickness is tripled. The difference in concentration does not change. By what factor does the rate of diffusion change?
questions.explanation: Rate ∝ area ÷ thickness here, so the factor is 2 ÷ 3 = 0.67. The extra thickness outweighs the extra area.

questions.stem: A cube of side 1 mm has a surface area of 6 mm², a volume of 1 mm³ and a surface area-to-volume ratio of 6. The side length is increased to 4 mm. What is the new surface area-to-volume ratio?

options.text: 6, because the surface area and the volume are both multiplied by four
1.5, because the area becomes 96 mm² and the volume becomes 64 mm³
24, because a larger cube has more surface, so the ratio rises fourfold
0.67, because it compares the 64 mm³ volume with the 96 mm² surface area

questions.explanation: Area = 6 × 4² = 96 mm²; volume = 4³ = 64 mm³; ratio = 96 ÷ 64 = 1.5. Area × 16, volume × 64: the ratio falls to a quarter.

questions.stem: The absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a has peaks at about 430 nm (blue) and 660 nm (red) but a trough at about 550 nm (green). Which statement best explains this pattern?

options.text: Green photons carry too little energy to excite an electron in chlorophyll a, whereas blue and red photons both carry more than enough energy to do so.
Chlorophyll a absorbs green light more strongly than any other colour, which is exactly why leaves that contain it appear green.
Blue and red light heat the chlorophyll molecule more than green light does, so more of their energy is taken in and stored.
Only photons whose energy matches that needed to excite an electron in chlorophyll a are absorbed; blue and red photons match, green do not.

questions.stem: Suppose that blood flow through the gill capillaries of an anaesthetised fish is stopped while water continues to flow over the gills, and that oxygen uptake across the gills falls almost to zero within a minute. Which explanation is best supported?

options.text: With no blood flow, oxygen built up in the stationary blood until its concentration matched the water's, so the gradient was lost.
Stopping blood flow cannot affect the gradient across the gill; the water flowing over the gills must have run out of oxygen.
Blood held still in the capillaries should load more fully, so the fall must have been caused by damage to the gill surface.
Oxygen enters with water absorbed into the blood, and once the blood stopped moving no more water could be taken up.

questions.stem: A hypothetical single-celled organism has the shape of a rectangular solid, 20 μm long, 10 μm high and 10 μm wide. What is the cell's surface area-to-volume ratio?

Illustrative data. On a paper chromatogram of leaf pigments, the origin line was 20 mm from the bottom edge of the paper, the centre of the carotene spot was 65 mm from the bottom edge and the solvent front was 70 mm from the bottom edge. What is the Rf value of carotene?
questions.explanation: Pigment: 65 − 20 = 45 mm. Solvent front: 70 − 20 = 50 mm. Rf = 45 ÷ 50 = 0.90.

questions.stem: Why is the surface of a gas-exchange organ kept moist?

options.text: The moisture is not needed for exchange; it only keeps the cells of the surface from drying out and dying.
The moisture forms a sticky layer that traps dust and pathogens before they reach the exchange surface.
Oxygen and carbon dioxide dissolve in the film of water before diffusing across the cell membranes.
The water is absorbed into the blood across the surface, carrying the dissolved oxygen in with it.

questions.explanation: Gases cross plasma membranes in solution, so moisture is a property of every gas-exchange surface.

questions.stem: Shrews are among the smallest mammals. Like larger mammals, they keep their body temperature nearly constant. A shrew must eat much more food per gram of its body mass each day than a deer does. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: A shrew's cells are much smaller than a deer's, so each has a higher SA:V and needs more food per gram.
A shrew's small body can store only a little heat, so it must eat often to refill that store.
A shrew uses more energy in total each day than a deer does, because its rate per gram of body mass is higher.
A shrew has a higher SA:V, so it loses heat faster per gram and needs more energy per gram to replace it.

questions.stem: Lungless salamanders have no lungs and, as adults, no gills. They exchange gases across their skin and the lining of the mouth. Which set of features would best suit this way of life?

options.text: Dry, thick skin, so that gases cross it as gases without having to dissolve first.
Thin, moist skin over a dense capillary network, with blood flowing through it continuously.
A large, bulky body, so that the total area of skin available for gas exchange is as large as possible.
Slow blood flow through the skin, so that each red blood cell has time to fill with oxygen.

questions.stem: A spherical single-celled organism grows from a radius of 10 µm to a radius of 30 µm, keeping its shape. Which prediction is best supported?

options.text: Its SA:V rises to three times the original, so each unit of volume is better supplied.
Its SA:V is unchanged, because its shape has not changed.
Its surface grows ninefold, so supply now easily exceeds its larger needs.
Its SA:V falls to one third, so less surface serves each unit of volume.

questions.explanation: SA:V goes from 0.30 to 0.10 µm⁻¹. Demand grows × 27; supply surface only × 9.
